items.title: Lisa Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 22, 2021
items.q: then all the way through to say Butch Morris

ctx.x: What did you get from Tommy Newsom? A hand-written —

Hand-written big score, and I ended up doing a ton of stuff for Tommy. And he, I learnt the ethics of copying from Tommy. He told me some great stories. After the very first one I’m like, “So Tommy, I don’t know whether to ask you, sometimes I know there’s a missing flat but I know it’s all in unison, do you want me to ask you about that or what’s the ethics here? What should I do here? And in answer he said, “When Duke Ellington was trying out a new copyist he would put two mistakes in the chart and expect the…

Did you ever get — well this would have maybe not been able to happen — a recording of the song in some form which would inform you about the arrangement and whether or not the arranger really — I can’t finish my question. I’m just wondering you know if you heard a recording, perhaps a combo arrangement of something that then became a big band arrangement, might you have heard something in the combo that didn’t seem to be jiving in the arrangement, and then have to bring that up with the arranger?
